claims.sentence_span: The study under review investigates a transfer learning strategy for classifying Parkinson's disease (PD) from speech across three languages: Spanish, German, and Czech ([Document 1](document_1.txt)).

claims.subject: study
claims.sentence_span: The study uses three language-specific datasets: a Spanish dataset based on the PC-GITA corpus, a German dataset, and a Czech dataset ([Document 2](document_2.txt)).

claims.subject: Spanish dataset
claims.sentence_span: The participants were asked to perform a relatively broad set of speech tasks: they pronounced a total of 10 sentences, rapidly repeated the syllables /pa-ta-ka/, /pe-ta-ka/, /pa-ka-ta/, /pa/, /ta/, and /ka/, read one text with 36 words, and produced a monologue ([Document 1](document_1.txt)).

claims.subject: earlier phonation analysis study
claims.sentence_span: For example, earlier work proposed a phonation analysis based on time-frequency representations to assess tremor in PD speech, using classifiers such as Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) and support vector machines (SVMs), with accuracies up to 77% on utterances from PC-GITA ([Document 1](document_1.txt)).

claims.sentence_span: The German dataset is also important in the transfer learning results because a model trained on Spanish utterances was used to fine-tune a model for classifying German PD utterances, yielding an accuracy improvement of up to 8% ([Document 1](document_1.txt)).
